title: Cycle detection — undirected and directed
summary: Undirected: a visited neighbour that is not your parent means a cycle. Directed: a neighbour that is still on the current DFS path (state "visiting") means a cycle.

sections.title: Undirected graphs
sections.body:
✍️ DFS passing the parent. Reaching an already-visited vertex that is **not the parent** means there is another path to it → cycle.
✍️ Union-find alternative: for each edge (u, v), if u and v are already in the same set, this edge closes a cycle ([[graph-dsu]]). This is Redundant Connection.

sections.title: Directed graphs: three states
Kahn's algorithm also detects cycles
sections.body: ✍️ Topological sort by in-degrees processes every vertex iff the graph is acyclic. If fewer than n vertices were processed, there is a cycle ([[graph-topological-sort#kahn]]).

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.body: Course schedule (can you finish all courses?), find eventual safe states (vertices not leading to a cycle = those that reach state 2), redundant connection, detect deadlock.
